title: Communication Foundations
description: Build core spoken/written English from the ground up: greet, introduce yourself, narrate, give opinions, argue, and handle questions. A1 to B2.

nodes.title: Greetings and Names
nodes.skill: Greet someone, give your name, and say where you are from.
nodes.teach_focus: The fixed frames 'Hello, I am ___' and 'I am from ___'; the capital I.
nodes.success_criteria: A greeting with your name, plus one sentence saying where you are from.
nodes.bridge_focus: Just the name frame: 'Hello, I am ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: Hello, ___ name is Priya.
bridge_exercises.hint: the small word before 'name' that shows it belongs to you
bridge_exercises.context: Locks the 'My name is ___' opener before any free greeting.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: my

bridge_exercises.sentence: Hi, I ___ Arjun.
bridge_exercises.hint: the verb 'to be' for 'I' in the present (one word)
bridge_exercises.context: The 'I am ___' frame for giving your own name.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: am

bridge_exercises.sentence: I am ___ India.
bridge_exercises.hint: a small word that goes before a place to show where you come from
bridge_exercises.context: Adds 'I am from ___' so the learner can say where they are from.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: from

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which is a complete, polite greeting with your name?
bridge_exercises.hint: Pick the full sentence, not just one or two words.
bridge_exercises.context: Checks the learner can recognise a complete greeting before producing one.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Hello, my name is Sara.
options: Hello, my name is Sara.
Hello name Sara.
Sara hello me.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Say hello, tell me your name, and say which city or country you are from.
bridge_exercises.hint: Two short sentences: 'Hello, I am ___.' and 'I am from ___.'
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the greeting, name, and origin the node targets.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Hello, I am Sneha. I am from Jaipur, India.

exemplars: Hello, my name is Ravi. I am from Chennai.
Hi, I am Aisha and I am from Lucknow.

nodes.title: Introduce Yourself
nodes.skill: Frame a clear 2-sentence self-introduction (name, role, one detail).
nodes.teach_focus: Subject-verb basics in the present tense; one concrete detail.
nodes.success_criteria: Two grammatical sentences: who they are + one specific fact.
nodes.bridge_focus: Just one sentence: 'My name is ___ and I ___.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: My name ___ Ravi and I am a nurse.
bridge_exercises.hint: verb 'to be', present simple, third person singular
bridge_exercises.context: Locks the core 'My name is ___' frame before the learner attempts a free self-intro.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: is

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which sentence adds one clear personal detail after your name and role?
bridge_exercises.hint: Pick the option with a single concrete fact, not a vague phrase.
bridge_exercises.context: Moves from the bare frame toward the 'one specific fact' success criterion.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: I'm a teacher, and I love reading historical novels.
options: I'm a teacher, and I love reading historical novels.
I'm a teacher and many things, you know.
I'm a teacher, nice, good, etc.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Introduce yourself in two sentences: say your name and role, then one specific detail about you.
bridge_exercises.hint: Sentence one: name + role. Sentence two: one real fact (a hobby, a city, a goal).
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the full two-sentence intro the node targets.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Hi, I'm Sneha and I'm a software engineer. In my free time I'm learning to play the guitar.

exemplars: Hi, I'm Anil. I'm a second-year commerce student, and I love cricket and cooking.
My name is Meera and I work as a graphic designer. I just moved to Pune last month.

nodes.title: Describe Your Routine
nodes.skill: Use the present simple to describe habitual actions in sequence.
nodes.teach_focus: Present-simple conjugation; sequencing words (first, then, after).
nodes.success_criteria: 3+ sequenced present-tense actions, correct verb forms.
nodes.bridge_focus: One present-tense sentence about a single daily action.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Every morning she ___ coffee before she starts work.
bridge_exercises.hint: present simple, third person singular of 'drink'
bridge_exercises.context: Anchors correct present-simple conjugation on a single habitual action.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: drinks

bridge_exercises.sentence: I wake up at seven. ___ I brush my teeth, and then I have breakfast.
bridge_exercises.hint: a sequencing word that means 'as the first step'
bridge_exercises.context: Introduces sequencing words that string habitual actions into order.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: First

bridge_exercises.sentence: Describe your morning routine in at least three present-tense actions, using sequencing words like first, then, and after.
bridge_exercises.hint: Use present simple throughout and connect the steps in order.
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the full sequenced routine the node targets.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: First I wake up and check my phone. Then I make tea and read the news. After that, I go for a short walk.

exemplars: Every day I get up at six, then I go for a run, and after that I take a shower and start work.
First I make breakfast for my family. Then I drop my son at school, and after that I open my shop.

nodes.title: Narrate a Past Event
nodes.skill: Narrate a completed event using the past tense.
nodes.teach_focus: Regular vs irregular past forms; time markers (yesterday, last week).
nodes.success_criteria: A short past-tense narration with correct verb forms.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Yesterday I ___ to the market and bought some vegetables.
bridge_exercises.hint: irregular past tense of 'go'
bridge_exercises.context: Drills an irregular past form on the node's core 'Yesterday I ___' frame.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: went

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which sentence correctly narrates a completed past event?
bridge_exercises.hint: Find the one with a correct past form and a time marker.
bridge_exercises.context: Tests recognition of correct regular/irregular past forms with time markers.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Last week we visited my grandparents and stayed two nights.
options: Last week we visited my grandparents and stayed two nights.
Last week we visit my grandparents and stay two nights.
Last week we will visit my grandparents and stay two nights.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Tell the story of something you did last weekend in three or four past-tense sentences.
bridge_exercises.hint: Use a time marker like 'last Saturday' and keep all verbs in the past.
bridge_exercises.context: Free past-tense narration matching the node's success criterion.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Last Saturday I met two old friends. We had lunch at a small cafe and then watched a film. After that, we walked along the river for an hour.

exemplars: Yesterday I finished my project and sent it to my manager. Then I celebrated with my team over dinner.
Last month I travelled to Goa with my cousins. We swam in the sea every day and tried a lot of new food.

nodes.title: State an Opinion
nodes.skill: State an opinion with a supporting reason.
nodes.teach_focus: 'I think/believe ... because ...' framing; one clear reason.
nodes.success_criteria: An opinion + at least one relevant supporting reason.

bridge_exercises.sentence: I think reading is useful ___ it builds your vocabulary.
bridge_exercises.hint: linking word that introduces a reason
bridge_exercises.context: Locks the 'opinion + because + reason' frame the node is built on.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: because

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which response states an opinion and backs it with a relevant reason?
bridge_exercises.hint: Look for both an opinion and a reason that actually supports it.
bridge_exercises.context: Distinguishes a supported opinion from a bare one or an off-topic reason.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: I believe remote work is better because it saves hours of commuting time.
options: I believe remote work is better because it saves hours of commuting time.
I believe remote work is better. The weather is nice today.
Remote work, yes, maybe, it is a thing people do.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Give your opinion on whether students should learn to code at school, and support it with one clear reason.
bridge_exercises.hint: Start with 'I think' or 'I believe', then give one reason after 'because'.
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of a supported opinion on a fresh topic.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: I think students should learn to code at school because it teaches logical thinking that helps in almost any career.

exemplars: I think public libraries are important because they give everyone free access to knowledge.
I believe walking to work is better than driving because it keeps you healthy and saves money.

nodes.title: Compare Two Things
nodes.skill: Compare two options using comparative structures.
nodes.success_criteria: A clear comparison naming a difference and a preference.
nodes.bridge_focus: One comparative sentence: 'A is ___er than B.'

bridge_exercises.sentence: Trains are usually ___ than buses for long journeys.
bridge_exercises.hint: comparative form of 'fast' using -er
bridge_exercises.context: Drills the core '-er than' comparative frame the node targets.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: faster

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which sentence compares two options correctly with a longer adjective?
bridge_exercises.hint: Long adjectives take 'more', not '-er'.
bridge_exercises.context: Builds the 'more/less ... than' comparative for adjectives that cannot take -er.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: A laptop is more expensive than a tablet.
options: A laptop is more expensive than a tablet.
A laptop is expensiver than a tablet.
A laptop is more expensive that a tablet.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Compare living in a big city and a small town. Name one clear difference and say which you prefer.
bridge_exercises.hint: Use a comparative like 'busier than' or 'more relaxed than', then state your preference.
bridge_exercises.context: Free comparison naming a difference and a preference, as the criterion requires.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: A big city is busier and more crowded than a small town, but I prefer the city because it offers more job opportunities.

exemplars: Tea is cheaper than coffee, but I prefer coffee because it gives me more energy in the morning.
Online classes are more flexible than classroom lessons, though I prefer the classroom because I focus better there.

nodes.title: Make a Short Argument
nodes.skill: Build a 3-part argument: claim, reason, example.
nodes.teach_focus: Claim -> reason -> concrete example structure; linking words.
nodes.success_criteria: A claim backed by a reason and a concrete example.
nodes.bridge_focus: State only the claim in one sentence; reasons come later.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Cycling to work is good for the city. ___, it reduces traffic and pollution.
bridge_exercises.hint: two-word linking phrase that introduces a concrete example
bridge_exercises.context: Anchors the linking phrase that signals the 'example' part of the argument.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: For example

bridge_exercises.sentence: Which version is a complete claim-reason-example argument?
bridge_exercises.hint: It must have all three parts: a claim, a reason, and a concrete example.
bridge_exercises.context: Tests whether the learner can recognise a full three-part argument.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Schools should teach budgeting because students manage money badly; for example, many graduates fall into debt within a year.
options: Schools should teach budgeting because students manage money badly; for example, many graduates fall into debt within a year.
Schools should teach budgeting. It is a good idea overall.
Budgeting, money, students, debt, very important topic.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Argue that companies should allow a four-day work week. Give your claim, one reason, and one concrete example.
bridge_exercises.hint: Structure it as: claim, then 'because' for the reason, then 'for example' for the example.
bridge_exercises.context: Free production of the full claim-reason-example argument the node targets.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Companies should allow a four-day work week because rested employees are more productive. For example, when one firm in Iceland tried it, output stayed the same while staff felt far less burned out.

exemplars: Cities should add more bike lanes because they cut pollution. For example, after Paris expanded its lanes, car use in the centre dropped sharply.
Students should learn first aid in school because it saves lives. For example, a classmate of mine once helped a choking passenger because she had been trained.

nodes.title: Handle a Follow-up Question
nodes.skill: Answer an unexpected follow-up directly and concisely.
nodes.success_criteria: A direct, on-topic answer to the follow-up, no padding.
nodes.bridge_focus: Answer in a single sentence, then stop.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Interviewer: 'Why did you leave your last job?' Which reply is direct and concise?
bridge_exercises.hint: Pick the answer that addresses the question and then stops.
bridge_exercises.context: Trains the 'answer directly, then stop' behaviour against a padded alternative.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: I left to take on a role with more responsibility.
options: I left to take on a role with more responsibility.
Well, it's a long story, there were many things, the team, the office, the commute, honestly so much happened.
That's a good question and I really appreciate you asking it, thank you so much.

bridge_exercises.sentence: When you don't know the exact figure, you can say: 'I'm not sure of the exact number, ___ I can find out and send it today.'
bridge_exercises.hint: linking word that pivots to what you CAN do
bridge_exercises.context: Models acknowledging a gap and answering helpfully without rambling.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: but

bridge_exercises.sentence: Someone asks: 'What's the biggest weakness in your plan?' Acknowledge it briefly, answer in one or two sentences, and then stop.
bridge_exercises.hint: Acknowledge, give one honest weakness plus how you'd handle it, then stop talking.
bridge_exercises.context: Free practice of the acknowledge-answer-stop pattern under an unexpected follow-up.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Good question. The biggest risk is the tight timeline, so I've built in a one-week buffer to absorb delays.

exemplars: Honestly, the main challenge was the budget, so we cut two features to stay on track.
I'm not certain of the exact date, but I can confirm it by tomorrow morning.

nodes.title: Speak Your Introduction
nodes.skill: Deliver the self-introduction aloud with clear pacing.
nodes.teach_focus: Pace and pausing; apply the text framing under voice.
nodes.success_criteria: Two to three complete sentences giving name, role, and one specific personal fact, delivered as a paced spoken intro (full sentences, no fragments).
nodes.bridge_focus: Say only your name and role aloud.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Say only your name and role aloud, clearly and slowly: 'Hi, I'm ___ and I'm a ___.'
bridge_exercises.hint: Speak slowly, pause after your name, and keep it to one breath.
bridge_exercises.context: The bridge_focus task: warm up the voice with just name and role before a full intro.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Hi, I'm Karan and I'm a marketing analyst.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Now say your full two-sentence introduction aloud at a steady pace, pausing briefly between the two sentences.
bridge_exercises.hint: Pause where a comma or full stop would go; don't rush the second sentence.
bridge_exercises.context: Applies the text self-intro framing under voice with controlled pacing.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Hi, I'm Karan and I'm a marketing analyst. I've been learning data tools recently, and I really enjoy turning numbers into stories.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Give your full introduction aloud — name, role, and one interesting thing about you — at a calm, even pace with a clear pause between each sentence.
bridge_exercises.hint: Three short sentences; pause where a full stop goes, and don't rush or freeze.
bridge_exercises.context: Stretches the learner to deliver a complete, well-paced spoken intro — the node's success criterion under full voice control.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: Hi, I'm Karan and I'm a marketing analyst. I've spent the last year learning data tools. Outside work, I run a small food blog that keeps my writing sharp.

exemplars: Hi, I'm Priya and I'm a final-year engineering student. I love building small robots in my free time.
Hello, my name is Sahil and I work as a chef. I specialise in South Indian food and I'm learning Italian cooking now.

nodes.title: Hold a Short Exchange
nodes.skill: Sustain a short back-and-forth aloud without freezing.
nodes.teach_focus: Turn-taking; quick formulation under live pressure.
nodes.success_criteria: At least three on-topic turns that sustain a back-and-forth — each a complete response, with at least one question returned to the other speaker — and no turn left abandoned.
nodes.bridge_focus: Answer one spoken question, then ask one back.

bridge_exercises.sentence: I ask: 'What do you do on weekends?' Answer aloud in one sentence, then ask me the same question back.
bridge_exercises.hint: Answer, then turn the question around with 'And you?' or 'What about you?'
bridge_exercises.context: The bridge_focus task: one answer plus one return question to start turn-taking.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: On weekends I usually meet friends and watch a film. What about you?

bridge_exercises.sentence: You need a second to think mid-conversation. Which is the best way to keep your turn without freezing?
bridge_exercises.hint: A natural filler buys time; a long silence loses your turn.
bridge_exercises.context: Teaches recoverable hesitation, a key part of the success criterion.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: That's a good question, let me think for a second.
options: That's a good question, let me think for a second.
(stay completely silent for ten seconds)
Um, um, um, um, um, um, um, um.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Hold a three-turn exchange aloud about your favourite food: answer my question, ask one back, and respond to my reply, staying on topic.
bridge_exercises.hint: Keep each turn short, stay on the food topic, and recover smoothly from any pauses.
bridge_exercises.context: Full multi-turn exchange matching the 3+ on-topic spoken turns criterion.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: My favourite food is biryani because of the spices. What's yours? Oh, pasta is great too, do you cook it yourself or order it?

exemplars: I love hiking on Sundays. How about you? Nice, I've never tried rock climbing, is it hard to start?
My favourite city is Jaipur because of the old forts. Which place do you like most? Oh, Kerala sounds beautiful, when did you go?

nodes.title: Recover Under Interruption
nodes.skill: Stay coherent when interrupted and regain the thread.
nodes.teach_focus: Reset phrases; finish the point after an interruption.
nodes.success_criteria: Handles an interruption and completes the original point.
nodes.bridge_focus: After an interruption, restate your last sentence.

bridge_exercises.sentence: You were mid-point when someone cut in. Which reset phrase best lets you regain the thread?
bridge_exercises.hint: A good reset phrase acknowledges the cut and steers back to your point.
bridge_exercises.context: Equips the learner with a reset phrase, the node's core teach_focus.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: As I was saying, the main issue is the deadline.
options: As I was saying, the main issue is the deadline.
Okay, never mind, forget my point.
Sorry, sorry, I'll just stop talking then.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Say this sentence aloud: 'The plan needs more testing time.' I will interrupt you. After my interruption, restate your last sentence and continue.
bridge_exercises.hint: Use a short reset like 'As I was saying' and then repeat your point.
bridge_exercises.context: The bridge_focus task: restate your last sentence after being interrupted.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: As I was saying, the plan needs more testing time, otherwise we risk shipping bugs.

bridge_exercises.sentence: Explain why your team missed a deadline. I will interrupt you partway through. Acknowledge the interruption, then finish your original point clearly.
bridge_exercises.hint: Handle the cut-in briefly, reset with a phrase, and complete the point you started.
bridge_exercises.context: Full pressure scenario: stay coherent through an interruption and complete the point.
bridge_exercises.answer_key: We missed the deadline because a key supplier was late. Sure, I'll come to costs in a moment, but to finish my point first: once the parts arrived, we actually shipped within two days.

exemplars: Good point, I'll address that next, but as I was saying, the root cause was the data migration.
Let me just finish this thought first: the budget held steady. Now, to your question about staffing...
